bottom_line: In patients with drug-eluting stents, continued thienopyridine therapy (vs. placebo) reduced stent thrombosis (0.4% vs. 1.4%; hazard ratio, 0.29 [95% CI, 0.17 to 0.48]).
implications: The reported data support that, from 12 to 30 months, continuing thienopyridine (vs. placebo) lowers stent thrombosis (0.4% vs. 1.4%; hazard ratio, 0.29 [95% CI, 0.17 to 0.48]) and major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (4.3% vs. 5.9%; hazard ratio, 0.71 [95% CI, 0.59 to 0.85]) but increases moderate or severe bleeding (2.5% vs. 1.6%). These numbers also indicate all-cause death was 2.0% vs. 1.5% (hazard ratio, 1.36 [95% CI, 1.00 to 1.85]; P = 0.05), and the document notes an elevated risk of stent thrombosis and myocardial infarction in both groups in the 3 months after thienopyridine discontinuation.

major_points.text: Patients were randomized after completing 12 months of thienopyridine plus aspirin, to continue thienopyridine or switch to placebo for 18 months; aspirin was continued in both groups.
major_points.quote: After 12 months of treatment with a thienopyridine drug (clopidogrel or prasugrel) and aspirin, patients were randomly assigned to continue receiving thienopyridine treatment or to receive placebo for another 18 months; all patients continued receiving aspirin.
A total of 9961 patients were randomly assigned to continue thienopyridine treat- ment or to receive placebo.

major_points.text: Copri mary efficacy end points were stent thrombosis and major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (death, MI, or stroke) from 12 to 30 months.
major_points.quote: The coprimary efficacy end points were stent thrombosis and major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (a compos- ite of death, myocardial infarction, or stroke) during the period from 12 to 30 months.

major_points.text: Continued thienopyridine reduced stent thrombosis compared with placebo.
major_points.quote: reduced the rates of stent thrombosis (0.4% vs. 1.4%; hazard ratio, 0.29 [95% confidence interval {CI}, 0.17 to 0.48]; P<0.001)

major_points.text: Continued thienopyridine reduced major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events compared with placebo.
major_points.quote: major adverse car- diovascular and cerebrovascular events (4.3% vs. 5.9%; hazard ratio, 0.71 [95% CI, 0.59 to 0.85]; P<0.001).

major_points.text: Myocardial infarction was lower with continued thienopyridine than with placebo.
major_points.quote: The rate of myocardial infarction was lower with thieno- pyridine treatment than with placebo (2.1% vs. 4.1%; hazard ratio, 0.47; P<0.001).

major_points.text: Bleeding risk increased with continued thienopyridine.
major_points.quote: The rate of moderate or severe bleeding was increased with continued thi- enopyridine treatment (2.5% vs. 1.6%, P = 0.001).

major_points.text: An elevated risk of stent thrombosis and myocardial infarction was observed during the 3 months after stopping thienopyridine in both groups.
major_points.quote: An elevated risk of stent thrombo- sis and myocardial infarction was observed in both groups during the 3 months after discontinuation of thienopyridine treatment.

inclusion_criteria.text: Patients older than 18 years of age who were candidates for dual antiplatelet therapy after treatment with FDA-approved drug-eluting or bare-metal stents.
inclusion_criteria.quote: We enrolled patients older than 18 years of age who were candidates for dual antiplatelet therapy after treatment with FDA-approved drug-eluting or bare-metal stents.

inclusion_criteria.text: At 12 months, patients had not had a major adverse cardiovascular or cerebrovascular event, repeat revascularization, or moderate or severe bleeding and were adherent to thienopyridine therapy.
inclusion_criteria.quote: At 12 months, patients who had not had a major adverse cardio- vascular or cerebrovascular event, repeat revascu- larization, or moderate or severe bleeding and had been adherent to thienopyridine therapy

criticisms.text: Only adherent patients without major adverse events, stent thrombosis, or moderate/severe bleeding in the first year underwent randomization, potentially selecting lower-risk patients.
criticisms.quote: only patients who were adher- ent to therapy and who did not have a major adverse cardiovascular or cerebrovascular event, stent thrombosis, or moderate or severe bleeding in the first year underwent randomization

criticisms.text: The study did not quantify the net effect of ischemic and bleeding events.
criticisms.quote: although we did not quantify the net effect of ischemic and bleeding events

criticisms.text: Generalizability to other stent types or non-thienopyridine P2Y12 inhibitors is unknown.
criticisms.quote: whether the treatment benefits observed will be gener- alizable to other stent types30,31 or non-thieno- pyridine P2Y12 inhibitors32,33 is unknown.
